prior_importants.description: A PR closed on GitHub without merging is counted as an open PR forever. Its numbers stay taken permanently. If its gated sha is ever pruned, every ADR-adding gate in the repo fails, and nothing in the store can retire the PR.

findings.description: An open-PR peer whose pinned commit exists but cannot be diffed against the target is skipped with a note, and the stage still passes. The session being gated can cause this, for example by listing the pinned sha in the shared `.git/shallow`, which no pin covers. It can then land a decision number that the open PR already holds.
findings.body:
**A gated session can make an open PR's pinned commit undiffable, and the stage then passes the clash.**

The stage reads an open PR's decisions at the sha pup recorded, because a session could move either ref (ADR 0146). It also refuses when that commit is missing, because "passing would let a clash through unseen". The read-error path does not keep that promise. `peerDecisions` turns every git failure that is not a kill into a skip string, for every kind of peer:

```ts
} catch (error) {
  if (!isOverrun(error)) rethrowIfKilled(error);
  return 'git could not read it against the target';
}
```

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/a31ea13e70035f21915833ac72facc77045d2eb3/src/core/adr-number.service.ts#L152-L168>

The stage loop sends a string result to `unchecked` whether or not the peer has a `prUrl`. Only an `undefined` result (commit absent) reaches `unreadPrs`, and the stage status counts only refusals, `unreadPrs` and misnamed paths:

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/a31ea13e70035f21915833ac72facc77045d2eb3/src/core/adr-number.service.ts#L290-L310>

**Trigger.** Session B has an open PR adding `docs/adr/0140-b.md`. Session A also adds `0140-a.md`, then before it gates:
1. A writes B's pinned sha into `$GIT_COMMON_DIR/shallow`. Sessions can write the shared common dir (ADR 0089, first paragraph). `GIT_HISTORY_ENV` pins grafts and replace refs, but nothing pins `shallow` (ADR 0089 *Ceilings*).
2. `resolveCommitIfPresent` runs `rev-parse <sha>^{commit}`, which still succeeds, so this is not the missing-commit refusal.
3. `addedAdrPaths` runs the three-dot `git diff <target>...<sha>`. With no merge base it fails, the same failure the live-branch orphan test (`adr-number.test.ts` L186-207) pins as a skip.
4. The stage passes with `not checked against pup/B: …`, and both PRs carry 0140.

Deleting a loose tree object of the pinned commit has the same effect.

ADR 0089 accepted the unpinned shallow file only because "cutting can only remove a merge-base, which fails the diff rather than shrinking it". This catch is the first reader where a failed diff counts as a pass. ADR 0146's ceilings cover sessions moving the live `refs/heads/pup/*` and a pruned PR commit, which is refused. They do not cover a PR commit that is present but cannot be diffed. No test covers that case: the PR-peer tests (L256-293) cover only a missing sha, a malformed sha and a missing commit.

**Fix direction.** An open PR's head is fixed and was readable at its own gate, so a read failure for a peer with `prUrl` should be refused like a missing commit. Live branches keep the documented skip.
1. Have `peerDecisions` return a result the loop can tell apart from the more-than-three cap. Both are plain strings today.
2. Send that result to `unreadPrs` with its own wording. The current "fetch the PR's head here" line would be false when the commit is present.
3. Add a test that pins a parentless commit as an open PR's sha and expects a refusal.

process_issues.description: Round 4 budget: only correctness, security and guards ran. Skipped conventions, docs, context, simplicity and maintainability under the round budget. Skipped workflow-safety (no .github/workflows change) and spec (no closing issue or --spec). Correctness and security ran two instances each because the diff is past the size gate (428 source + 675 test lines). Correctness was split into adr-number.service.ts logic and gate/CLI/dashboard integration; security into git argv/config evasion and output/resource bounds. The review-consolidator was not spawned: only one finding survived, so there was nothing to group. The head is unchanged since the prior record (a31ea13), so the prior important stays unresolved.

The git-evasion instance and the validator could not spike git's shallow-file behaviour under static CI. The confirmed finding's git mechanics (shallow honoured despite GIT_GRAFT_FILE; a three-dot diff with no merge base fails) rest on pinned-version knowledge and on the repo's own orphan test, hence medium confidence.
